issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path and omits error scenarios such as failed registry installs, shadcn CLI versions older than 3.x not supporting the namespace, missing animate-spotlight causing an unstyled spotlight, or a missing simplex-noise dependency.

scenarios.name: hero-beams-spotlight-tailwind-v4
scenarios.rationale: B installs both components with the shadcn CLI (namespace and URL forms), defines `--animate-spotlight` and `@keyframes spotlight` in `@theme`, and uses a relative, overflow-hidden section with the heading at `z-10`, so it meets every rubric item. A hand-writes the components instead of installing them, which the rubric forbids. It does define the animation in `@theme inline` and does use a relative, overflow-hidden section with the heading at `z-10`.

scenarios.name: register-registry-and-add-moving-border
scenarios.rationale: Both cover init, the registries entry with the CLI 3.x requirement, and the direct URL alternative, but B also names the `duration` prop and has a more complete usage example, while A adds Vite setup that goes beyond the rubric; neither says there is no `aceternity` npm package.

scenarios.name: wavy-background-performance-setup
scenarios.rationale: A installs the Aceternity component (with simplex-noise), uses next/dynamic with ssr:false, honors prefers-reduced-motion, uses documented props, and notes the window-sized canvas for full-width use, while B skips the Aceternity package, avoids next/dynamic ssr:false on purpose, and writes a custom reimplementation that only partly matches the rubric.
